```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = "##", fig.align = "center")
```

# Generate Data

```{r data, message = FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(sn)
library(NNS)

set.seed(12345)
n = 1000
asset_1 = rsn(n, xi = -.5, omega = 1, alpha = 1)
asset_2 = rsn(n, xi = -.25, omega = 1.5, alpha = 1)
asset_3 = rsn(n, xi = 0, omega = 1.2, alpha = 1)
asset_4 = rsn(n, xi = 1, omega = 1.3, alpha = 1)
asset_5 = rsn(n, xi = 1.5, omega = 2, alpha = 1)

assets = setDT(list(asset_1, asset_2, asset_3, asset_4, asset_5))
colnames(assets) = paste0("Asset_", 1:5)

# Grid values
cutpoints = seq(min(assets), max(assets), length.out = 6)
```

# Plot

Grey dashed lines are the target value all UPM calculations are based off of
for each density and then averaged. This is analogous to the shifted
distribution $f_{\to a}(\cdot)$.

```{r plot, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 4.5}
cols <- c("black", "steelblue", "darkgreen", "orange", "red")
d <- lapply(assets, density)
plot(d[[1]], xlim = range(sapply(d, function(z) range(z$x))),
     ylim = c(0, max(sapply(d, function(z) max(z$y)))), col = cols[1],
     main = "density.default(x = asset_1)")
for (k in 2:5) lines(d[[k]], col = cols[k])
abline(v = cutpoints, lty = 2, col = "grey")
legend("topright", legend = paste("Asset", 1:5), col = cols, lty = 1, bty = "n")
```

# Generate Probabilities

rank_5 based on relative shifted densities measured from several lattice
points

```{r upm}
# UPM from min value
upms = apply(assets, 2, function(x) UPM(1, cutpoints, x))
upms = cbind(upms, rowSums(upms))
upms = upms / upms[, ncol(upms)]
upms = upms[complete.cases(upms), -ncol(upms)]

rank_5_probabilities = colMeans(upms)
rank_5_probabilities
```

# MC Verification

Sample each asset without replacement based on its winning probability. Each
column represents a race, and the row represents the asset's finishing order.

```{r races}
replicates = 1000
races = replicate(replicates, sample(paste0("Asset_", 1:5), 5, replace = FALSE,
                                     prob = rank_5_probabilities))
rownames(races) = paste0("Rank_", 5:1)
head(races[, 1:10])

Results = matrix(NA, 5, 5)
for (i in 1:5) {
  for (j in 1:5) {
    Results[i, (6 - j)] = sum(races[j, ] == colnames(assets)[i]) / replicates
  }
}
colnames(Results) = paste0("Rank_", 1:5)
rownames(Results) = paste0("Asset_", 1:5)
Results

# sanity check
rowSums(Results)
colSums(Results)
```

Ranks from your notebook with $\rho = 0$.

> **Note (2026).** Normalized degree-1 UPMs are shares of above-target
> deviation severity, not probabilities of winning a race. Sampling finishing
> orders with those same shares as weights reproduces the weights; it does not
> validate them as event frequencies. The finishing frequencies of jointly
> observed races follow (see `examples/example-corrections.md`).

# Sampling with Dependence

Alternatively we can just infer the probabilities from the ranks of the tuple
elements themselves...

```{r empirical}
empirical_samples = cbind(assets,
                          t(apply(assets, 1, function(x) colnames(assets)[order(x, decreasing = FALSE)])))
colnames(empirical_samples) = c(paste0("Asset_", 1:5),
                                paste0("Rank_", 1:5))
empirical_samples

Results = matrix(NA, 5, 5)
for (i in 1:5) {
  for (j in 6:10) {
    Results[i, (j - 5)] = sum(empirical_samples[, .SD, .SDcols = j] == colnames(assets)[i]) / n
  }
}
colnames(Results) = paste0("Rank_", 1:5)
rownames(Results) = paste0("Asset_", 1:5)
Results
```

# Increasing the empirical samples via meboot

If we have small samples, we can increase them using the maximum entropy
bootstrap which preserves the dependence structure within time series.

We started off with 1,000 observations, let's make it 10,000 using
$\rho = 0.95$ for each bootstrap replicate.

```{r meboot}
bootstraps = do.call(cbind, lapply(assets, function(x)
  as.vector(NNS.meboot(unlist(x), reps = 10, rho = .95)["replicates", ]$replicates)))

bootstrap_samples = cbind(bootstraps,
                          t(apply(bootstraps, 1, function(x) colnames(bootstraps)[order(x, decreasing = FALSE)])))

bootstrap_samples = data.table(bootstrap_samples)
colnames(bootstrap_samples) = c(paste0("Asset_", 1:5),
                                paste0("Rank_", 1:5))
bootstrap_samples

Results = matrix(NA, 5, 5)
for (i in 1:5) {
  for (j in 6:10) {
    Results[i, (j - 5)] = sum(bootstrap_samples[, .SD, .SDcols = j] == colnames(bootstraps)[i]) /
      nrow(bootstraps)
  }
}
colnames(Results) = paste0("Rank_", 1:5)
rownames(Results) = paste0("Asset_", 1:5)
Results
```

Expanding the number of bootstraps, here's 1e6 replicates:

```{r meboot-1e6}
bootstraps2 = do.call(cbind, lapply(assets, function(x)
  as.vector(NNS.meboot(unlist(x), reps = 1000, rho = .95)["replicates", ]$replicates)))

bootstrap_samples2 = cbind(bootstraps2,
                           t(apply(bootstraps2, 1, function(x) colnames(bootstraps2)[order(x, decreasing = FALSE)])))

bootstrap_samples2 = data.table(bootstrap_samples2)

Results = matrix(NA, 5, 5)
for (i in 1:5) {
  for (j in 6:10) {
    Results[i, (j - 5)] = sum(bootstrap_samples2[, .SD, .SDcols = j] == colnames(bootstraps2)[i]) /
      nrow(bootstraps2)
  }
}
colnames(Results) = paste0("Rank_", 1:5)
rownames(Results) = paste0("Asset_", 1:5)
Results
```
